title: Complex natural behavior is almost never best explained by constraints

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complex natural behavior is almost never best explained by constraints

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Almost none of the complex behavior seen in nature is best explained as the satisfaction of constraints, because finding a pattern that satisfies a constraint is usually far too difficult a computation to happen routinely in nature; explicit processes of evolution are the more plausible explanation.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But despite this, my strong suspicion is that of all the examples of complex behavior that we see in nature almost none can in the end best be explained in terms of constraints.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “The Problem of Satisfying Constraints” (from p. 342), p. 342. Scope: complex behavior in physical and other natural systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-16: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.19

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted cases can be studied, but the near-universal statement requires a representative inventory that does not exist. Its explanatory and computational language admits competing operationalizations. New comparative measurements and mechanistic records would be needed even after formalizing the terms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a representative census of complex natural phenomena and formal competing generative models based on equilibrium constraints versus explicit dynamics, then compare out-of-sample likelihood and computational cost. The claim would be supported if constraint models almost never provide the best account and their required search exceeds physically available computation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Best explained and complex are not uniquely operationalized.

Model fit cannot by itself establish the historical causal process.

No representative dataset links natural phenomena to adjudicated explanatory mechanisms.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational premise, that exact satisfaction of hard discrete constraints is not reached by casual search, can be checked on public benchmark instances. The natural-history quantifier has no dataset that enumerates phenomena and their best explanations, and predictive comparisons exist only for scattered case studies. The claim can be probed for particular systems and not as a statement about almost all complex behavior.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a pre-registered list of complex natural patterns, compare held-out predictive error of an explicit growth or evolution model with that of a constraint-satisfaction model, and separately measure how close random or locally improved configurations come to meeting the constraint. A large predictive gap in favor of explicit dynamics, together with search that stalls far from solutions, would support the claim on that list; the reverse would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Best explained is not fixed by predictive error alone, so rival explanations can be redrawn after the fact.

There is no census of complex natural behavior on which almost none could be counted.
